title: TF modules, Helm hooks, and upgrade patterns (draft)
content:
Context and goal:
This is a working draft that assembles patterns we've been experimenting with for private/VPC/on-prem CI/CD. Focus areas: Terraform module lifecycle hooks (pre/post apply steps), Helm chart upgrade patterns (preupgrade/postupgrade hooks and health gates), and how to wire Argo/GitOps pipelines to enforce image signing, SBOM, and staged rollouts in airgapped and non-airgapped environments. The aim is to converge on a small set of repeatable patterns that ops and platform teams can adopt for customer private deployments.

High-level principles (guiding constraints):
- No opaque manual steps in the happy path: CI should validate, sign, and publish artifacts before human intervention is required.
- Enforce artifact provenance: every image/prov must have cosign signatures and an SBOM.
- Terraform modules publish an immutably-versioned release in our internal registry; module upgrade paths must be explicit and include migration hooks.
- Helm upgrades must be observable: pre-upgrade checks, staged rollout (canary) where possible, and automated rollback on signal thresholds.
- Airgapped installs require mirrored registries + offline attestation flows; the CI must produce artifacts that are consumable by mirror tooling.

Notes on Terraform modules (lifecycle and hooks):
- Pattern: each private-deploy TF module exposes: "pre_apply_hook" and "post_apply_hook" variables (strings pointing to script locations in the repo or references to an ops job). The module itself should never run the hook but return metadata (e.g., terraform output map with hook refs) so the pipeline executes hooks in order.
- Rationale: keeps TF idempotent and declarative while keeping side-effects orchestrated in CI/CD (safer rollback).
- Recommended module outputs: module_version, upgrade_notes_url, migration_step_count, resource_providers (list), and a "compatibility_matrix" blob (string) for quick operator checks.
- Example usage (CI pseudocode):
  - run: terraform init && terraform plan -out=plan.tfplan
  - run: terraform show -json plan.tfplan > plan.json
  - parse plan.json for changed module versions; if module_version changes, run a job: ./scripts/run-module-hooks.sh pre ${module} ${old_version} ${new_version}
  - apply: terraform apply plan.tfplan
  - post hooks: ./scripts/run-module-hooks.sh post ${module} ${old_version} ${new_version}
- Hook responsibilities: DB migrations, pre-warm caches, rotate KMS keys for tenants if required, create provisioning artifacts consumed by Helm charts. Hooks must be idempotent and support --dry-run.

Helm chart upgrade patterns and hooks:
- Use Helm hooks sparingly; prefer Kubernetes-native readiness checks and separate orchestration jobs. When Helm hooks are necessary: use pre-upgrade/post-upgrade hooks with explicit timeout and idempotency.
- Chart layout convention: charts/
    - templates/
    - hooks/pre-upgrade-job.yaml (annotated helm.sh/hook: pre-upgrade)
    - hooks/post-upgrade-job.yaml
    - values.schema.json (strict validation for operator-provided overrides)
- Staged rollout pattern: for customer clusters with >=3 nodes we recommend an Argo Rollout (or kube deployment with maxUnavailable/partition) configuration. The Helm chart includes a feature flag: enableStagedUpgrade: true/false.
- Health gates (signals to consider):
    - pod readiness % (target >= 95%)
    - tail latency p99 for local inference pod (if available)
    - error rate spike (5xxs) over 1m window
    - CPU/GPU saturation above threshold
    - e2e smoke test success (see CI smoke tests below)
- If any gate fails during rollout, Argo/rollout should automatically pause and trigger a rollback job that reverts to previous image and runs a cleanup hook.

Image signing, SBOM, and artifact provenance:
- CI step order (recommended): build -> unit tests -> SBOM generation (syft) -> static scans (trivy) -> cosign sign -> push to registry -> create release metadata (JSON blob with digest, SBOM link, cosign sigs) -> publish to artifact index (internal).
- For airgapped: in addition to above, produce a tarball of image digest + signature + SBOM + release metadata that ops can hand to registry mirror tooling. Document exact mirror manifest format in a separate Confluence doc (linked_artifacts references).
- Cosign key management: do NOT use ephemeral signing keys in customer airgap handoffs. Instead, CI should produce a signed attestation using Redwoods' ephemeral CI key AND produce an operator-mutable attest key placeholder that customer infra will re-sign with their HSM after mirror ingestion. Document the re-sign flow.

CI pipeline examples (GitHub Actions / GitLab pseudosteps):
- job: build-and-sign
  - checkout
  - build image -> tag with semver+sha
  - run unit tests
  - syft -o json > sbom.json
  - trivy image --exit-code 1 || (if new vuln, fail and create ticket)
  - cosign sign --key $COSIGN_KEY image@sha256:...
  - push image to registry
  - upload artifacts (sbom.json, cosign.sig) to artifact store
  - generate release metadata file and post to infra repo (PR against release index)

Argo/GitOps wiring:
- Argo should watch a releases repo that contains per-customer overlay (kustomize) pointing to pinned image digests.
- Promote flow: when CI publishes a release metadata blob, it raises a PR to the releases repo; the releases repo PR triggers Argo to pick up the new commit and start a deployment in the customer cluster (or wait for manual promotion depending on customer config).
- Use image digests only; never rely on mutable tags in private deployments.

Airgap-specific flows and registry mirrors:
- CI produces a "mirror bundle" tarball: images.tar + sbom.tar + sigs.tar + release-metadata.json. This bundle is scanned by an internal mirror tool that outputs a signed mirror manifest consumable by the customer's registry-sync operator.
- Mirror operator must validate cosign signature matches Redwoods' public key and optionally require the customer to re-sign with their key if policy requires.
- TODO: define exact mirror bundle layout and versioning strategy (bundle-v1, bundle-v2).

Testing and preflight checks (what CI must run before tagging a release for private deployment):
- unit tests, integration tests where possible (tiny inference smoke tests), security scans, SBOM production, cosign signature check, terraform plan dry-run, helm template linting, helm upgrade --install --dry-run, manifest validation (kubeval), and an e2e smoke job that exercises a local-kind/remote dev cluster deploying the chart and running a small inference query.
- Preflight gating in pipeline: all steps must pass or the release PR remains blocked. Provide human-readable failure logs and a one-click re-run for the failing stage.

Rollback and emergency remediation:
- Rollback strategy: two-tiered:
  1) Fast revert (image reversion to previous digest via Argo/Rollout) if health gates fail immediately.
  2) Full revert via terraform state rollback + helm chart rollback for breaking infra changes that require state migration reversal.
- Make sure terraform state backups are taken before major module upgrades and retained for at least 30 days for private deployments.
- Keep a documented incident playbook for "failed private upgrade" that includes steps for: scale-down consumer traffic, revert Argo manifest, run post-rollback cleanup hooks, restore DB snapshot if required.

Operational notes and unresolved questions:
- Who is the owner for module pre/post hooks? Ops or module author? Proposal: module author owns hook contract and provides a hook runner script; ops owns the runner environment and secrets.
- How do we safely migrate long-running DB stateful workloads during minor module upgrades? Need a migration staging environment or a canary customer path.
- Key rotation for cosign in private clusters: define an automated re-signing flow for mirrored images to avoid trust break in airgapped clusters.
- Metrics instrumentation: define a minimal set of rollout metrics (success_rate, rollback_count, avg_rollout_time, mean_time_to_recover) and wire them to the Redwood Console for private instances via a push gateway or sidecar connectors.

Immediate next steps (short action list):
- (Maya) Draft mirror-bundle-v1 layout and share — target 2025-03-25.
- (Liam) Prototype script for run-module-hooks.sh with dry-run support — target 2025-03-28.
- (Jinsoo) Add helm hooks template to the sample chart repo and test with Argo Rollouts — target 2025-04-04.
- (Ruth) Draft cosign re-signing operator proposal and KMS integration notes — target 2025-04-10.

References and links (internal):
- infra PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/321
- related Confluence: CONFLUENCE-PLAT-485 (module compatibility guidelines)
- Jira epic: JIRA-PRIVDEP-712 (private deploy release mechanics epic)

Notes to reviewers: this is intentionally a working sketch. Expect many small changes; call out any irreversible decisions (e.g., forcing all customers to use staged Argo Rollout vs. providing opt-in). Also flag any compliance/regulatory constraints that would block mirror re-sign flows.
